howDoI.q: How do I let the player climb into a vehicle?
How do I give a level a different character?
How do I make a vehicle that keeps moving when no key is held?
How do I make Up speed it up and Down slow it?
How do I make a river that flows by itself?
How do I make a key give a burst of speed?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Ride Along is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk, and in a vehicle they steer. Up and Down make a vehicle rise faster or slower. Space jumps on foot, does nothing in the rocket and is a paddle stroke in the canoe. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score.

Game-Maker has no vehicle. The rocket and the canoe are character files like the hero's, and a vehicle that never stops is only a character whose idle sequence moves. Nothing here hurts you.

pages.head: Level 1: Climb In
pages.html:
Level 1: Climb In

The path is flat. The first sign says what the hero can do on foot, and SPACE JUMPS UP TO THE LEDGE points at a ledge of four coins. At the end of the path a little rocket is parked on its fins. The WALK INTO THE ROCKET TO CLIMB IN sign points at it. Walk into it and the next level begins, with the helper inside.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The hero. Open ride.gam and pick level 1's scene. Its character slot names hero.chr and its character pictures hero.cbl, the same helper as in every Starter.
  • The ledge. It is a row of plank blocks, solid on top only, so a jump goes up through it and lands on it.
  • The rocket. It is two map blocks in one.map, rocketTop and rocketBottom, made like a door: nothing about them is solid. The link that ends the level starts on the bottom one, at the same spot where a door would be.
  • Climbing in. The link goes to level 2's scene. Nothing in the link mentions a rocket. The next scene's list of files does: its character slot names ship.chr.

pages.head: Level 2: Lift Off
pages.html:
Level 2: Lift Off

Press nothing and the rocket rises. A shaft of night sky, 16 blocks wide and 72 high, has signs along the way: IT RISES BY ITSELF, LEFT AND RIGHT STEER, UP IS FASTER, DOWN IS SLOWER. Gates of gray rock cross the shaft, each with a gap. Steer into the gap, and catch the gold stars on the way, worth 10 points each.

Fly straight at a gate and the rocket stops against the rock. It is not hurt, and its push does not stop: steer to the side and it is on its way again. The shaft closes in to a docking bay at the top. Touch the bay, and the next level begins.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The rocket. Level 2's scene names ship.chr and ship.cbl in the character slots. Open ship.chr in the character editor. It is a rocket with the helper's face in a round window, drawn as two blocks, one on top of the other, with a short flame that flickers between two pictures.
  • Rising by itself. This is the whole trick. Pick the Idle sequence, the one that runs when no key is held. It has four frames of one tick each, and every frame has a y of minus 2, so every tick it moves up 2 pixels. Each key's sequence has the same minus 2, so Left and Right steer 4 pixels across and the rocket keeps rising.
  • Faster and slower. Up's frames have a y of minus 4. Down's have minus 1, so it slows but never stops or sinks.
  • No jump. A jump is a sequence with a push upward. The rocket has none, and Space is given an empty sequence that moves as the idle one does.
  • No pull. The night-sky blocks have Gravity set to none. The Starter sky pulls down, and a pull down would hold the rocket back.
  • The rocks. rockA and rockB are solid on every side. The rocket's push goes on, but the engine does not move a character into a solid block, so it stays against the rock until you steer clear.
  • The bay. The row of bay blocks at the top is a link, like a door. There is one link from each open block of the bay's row, all to level 3, so touching any of them takes the rocket on. A scene has room for 20 links.

pages.head: Level 3: Down the River
pages.html:
Level 3: Down the River

A canoe with the helper paddling it floats on a river that runs up the screen. The river carries the canoe, a little slower than the rocket. Logs lie across the river with gaps to steer through, and pink lilies on green pads are worth 10 points each. Space is a paddle stroke, a short burst up the river. The river runs between two grassy banks and ends at a dock.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • The canoe. Level 3's scene names boat.chr and boat.cbl. The canoe is seen from above, and the helper's round beanie is in the middle of it.
  • The same trick. The Idle sequence moves up 1 pixel, then 2, then 1, then 2, so the river is a little slower than the rocket. The paddle is drawn at two angles, so it rocks as the canoe goes. Left and Right steer 3 pixels across; Up is 3 and Down is 1.
  • The stroke. Space is a sequence of six frames, each moving up 4 pixels, with splashes at the blades. Once per key press is on, so holding Space does not paddle for ever.
  • The water. water0, water1 and water2 are three pictures of the same water. Each turns into the next after 3 ticks (Next block and Time) and the last turns into the first, so the ripples slide up the screen at about the speed of the canoe.
  • Logs and banks. logL and logR make a log two blocks wide. They and the bank blocks are solid. lily gives 10 points and turns back into water.
  • Why not the water's gravity? A block with Gravity up does pull the canoe up, but it pulls a little harder every tick. In a test the canoe went from 2 pixels a tick to 11 in ten ticks, and 11 is as fast as any character can move. A river made that way is a fall, and steering at 3 pixels cannot fight it. Use block gravity for a short gust, as in Gusts, and a sequence's y for a steady drift.
  • The dock. It is the same as level 2's bay: a link from each open block of the row, to The End.

pages.head: What Game-Maker cannot do
pages.html:
What Game-Maker cannot do

A vehicle is only a character, and that has limits:

  • It cannot switch characters inside a scene. A scene names one character file. To get in, a link takes you to another scene that names the other file, which is why this game has a level for each.
  • It cannot scroll the world by itself. The screen follows the character, so the vehicle moves and the screen goes with it. The vehicle can be stopped by a solid block, and then the screen stops too.
  • It cannot slow the drift for just one stretch of the level. The drift is in the character file, so a scene that wants a different speed names a different file.
  • It cannot hurt a vehicle and bounce it back. A solid rock holds it, and a block that takes hit points hurts it, but nothing shoves it away.
  • A link starts from one block. A wide bay needs one link for each block of its row.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Change the rocket's Idle y from minus 2 to minus 3, in all four frames and in each key's sequence. It is quicker.
  • Give ship.chr's Space sequence a jump, with a momentum push upward, and the rocket can hop sideways over a rock.
  • Set a rock block's Hit points to minus 5 and it hurts instead of only stopping you.
  • Give boat.chr's Idle sequence a y of plus 1, and the canoe drifts down the screen instead: a river that flows the other way.
  • Draw a car or a skateboard in a new .cbl and make a level that names it.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.back: A small explorer climbs into a rocket that rises all by itself. Steer between the rocks, catch the stars and dock at the top, then take a canoe down a river that flows the same way. Each ride is a character file of its own. Play it, then open the game in Game-Maker and build your own.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
A vehicle is a character file that moves without a key
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: Three short levels about a ride that keeps moving by itself. On foot, a small explorer walks into a parked rocket. The next level names a different character file: the rocket rises on its own, even when no key is held, and the arrows only steer it past rocks and between stars. The last level does the same trick in a canoe on a river that flows up the screen. Signs in the levels say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and make your own.

57.long: On foot: jump. In the rocket: nothing, a rocket does not jump. In the canoe: a paddle stroke, a short burst of speed up the river.

72.long: On foot: climb up a ladder. In the rocket and the canoe: rise faster.

75.long: Walk left on foot; steer the rocket or the canoe left. The vehicle keeps rising while you steer.

77.long: Walk right on foot; steer the rocket or the canoe right. The vehicle keeps rising while you steer.

80.long: On foot: climb down a ladder. In the rocket and the canoe: rise more slowly, but never stop and never sink.

1.long: Jump on foot, paddle in the canoe.

sounds.9: The jump and the paddle stroke
